Subject: Re: LegacyBank - On‑prem Airgapped Deployment: hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi Mike / team —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand LegacyBank's air-gapped goals and the offline-ops constraints. Per our discussion, I pulled together a short recap and next steps so we have an agreed checklist before we escalate to engineering for a hardware quote and offline ops runbook.

Recap (high level):
- Deployment mode: Private on-prem, fully air-gapped (no outbound egress from compute nodes).
- Critical requirements: KMS integration via HSM/KMS appliance in DMZ, isolated spool for model updates, strict maintenance windows, and no external p2p update channel.
- Scale target: pilot ~3 inference nodes (16x A100-class equiv) for 2 QPS peak, plan for 30-node scale after validation.

Action items (owner / date):
1) Marissa (Redwood): send hardware compatibility / offline-ops checklist + sample runbook — today (attached).
2) IT Ops (LegacyBank): confirm whether vendor will allow rack-level remote hands during maintenance windows, and confirm preferred HSM vendor (Thales vs Azure Key Vault appliance) — by 3/15.
3) Mike (LegacyBank): share current procurement lead contact & any existing internal SOPs for air-gapped software updates — by 3/16.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf (capabilities + hardware guidance), hardware_offline_ops_checklist.xlsx (checklist we reviewed).

If that looks right, I'll open a workspace in our Secure Share and loop in Stéphanie (deployment PM) and Logan (solutions engineer) to scope the hardware sizing and offline update flow.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and attachments. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side after reviewing the checklist:

1) Hardware compatibility: when you say \"16x A100-class equiv\" for each inference node, can you indicate expected rack U and power draw per node? We're limited to 3U per compute appliance in our current data center pod.
2) Offline updates: can you confirm the distribution format for model updates? We require an MD5/SHA256 signed bundle and prefer to pull via a controlled USB transfer into an internal staging node. Does Redwood support signing bundles and an offline bundle format?

I'll confirm remote-hands policy and HSM vendor preference by 3/15. Procurement lead is included on the next reply.

Thanks,
Mike Turner
Sr. Manager, IT Infrastructure
LegacyBank

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LegacyBank - On‑prem Airgapped Deployment: hardware & offline ops follow-up

Mike — great questions. Quick answers below and some follow-ups for our infra team: 

1) Node footprint & power: our typical on-prem inference appliance (recommended reference) targets 2U–4U depending on card density. For the 16x A100-class configuration we quoted in the checklist, plan for ~3U and ~3.2–3.8kW under full load per chassis. We'll work with your datacenter floorplan constraints to propose a compatible chassis (we can drop to 8x cards per node and scale horizontally if you prefer lower per-chassis power).

2) Offline bundle format & signing: yes — Redwood supports signed model bundles (SHA256) and can produce a tarball with a detached signature. We also support a USB ingestion workflow for an internal staging node; our offline update runbook includes checksum verification, signature validation, and staged KV cache warm-up steps.

Next steps from Redwood engineering:
- Stephanie (cc'd) will scope the hardware variants (16x vs 8x configs) and produce a short TCO estimate.
- Logan (cc'd) will draft the offline bundle runbook including exact CLI commands, verification steps, and retry semantics.

I've attached the checklist again for your reference. If you can share procurement contact (and any procurement lead email), we'll open a procurement folder and start a formal quote.

Best,
Marissa

Quick internal note / update —

Marissa / team, I chatted with Solutions about the two chassis profiles. Draft summary:
- 16x card chassis (3U, ~3.5kW): best for density; fewer nodes to manage but higher per-chassis power/cooling needs.
- 8x card chassis (2U, ~1.9kW): slightly larger cluster but lower per-chassis power and fits more datacenter footprints.

I'll run a short TCO comparison and include example pricing/rack layout. Logan will draft the offline bundle runbook tomorrow and include the exact signature verification commands and example tarball structure.

Marissa — can you confirm whether LegacyBank requires FIPS-certified signing toolchain or just SHA256 detached signatures? If FIPS is required, we'll include that in the quote.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Product Deployment Manager, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Stephanie / Logan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed answers. Procurement lead is Sarah Jansen (sarah.jansen@legacybank.com) — I've CC'd her on this thread.

On FIPS: CISO has confirmed we require FIPS-validated signing for production bundles; dev pilot may use plain SHA256.

Next steps from our side:
- Procurement (Sarah) will coordinate a formal RFQ and share expected timelines.
- IT Ops will confirm remote-hands allowances by 3/22.
- We are happy to kick off a 4-week pilot on an 8x-card chassis if Redwood can provide a pilot quote and an example offline bundle for our staging process.

Please send the pilot quote and the draft runbook (Logan) to procurement and me; we'll setup a pilot scoping call next week.

Appreciate it —
Mike
Sr. Manager, IT Infrastructure, LegacyBank
